maps.name: Angoville
maps.description: The small farming community of Angoville has the potential to be the staging ground of a short but bloody battle. Open fields in the west would allow the swift movement of large squadrons unhindered by the terrain. Medics pray that the shelter found on the eastern end would be enough to hold off an Axis offensive that would surely prove fatal for the wounded too weak for transportation. The farmhouses to the east have been long abandoned, farmers fearing the impending conflict.

maps.name: Beach Assault
maps.description: From the beach up to the trenches this little corner of Normandy has seen a lot of action. The area is tight like the quartermaster’s  purse strings so you'll have a hard time maneuvering  but at least you won't get lost.

maps.name: Beaux Lowlands
maps.description: Rugged hills and thick forests separated by small patches of farming and green pasture dot the terrain in the region of Beaux.  As harsh as the landscape is, fighting amongst the Allied and Axis forces is even more unforgiving, as quick confrontations and close-quarters skirmishes are the order of the day.

maps.name: Bernieres-Sur-Mer
maps.description: Early on the morning of June 6th, 1944 the small, quiet coastal town of Bernieres-Sur-Mer woke to find itself deeply mired in one of the greatest invasions ever seen. Villagers were surprised to hear the invading soldiers speaking French - French Canadians of Le Régiment de la Chaudière.

maps.name: Best
maps.description: I'd like to say that Best is jammed between a rock and a hard place, but it's not. It's jammed between a wet place and a wetter place. Canals and rivers mean bridges, and bridges mean control.

maps.name: Carpiquet
maps.description: The airfield at Carpiquet is critical link for the Allied assault on the Axis forces in northern France.  However, the costs will be high to capture the airfield.  Located on high ground and surrounded by forest, the area can be easily defended.  Open fields to the east and south of the airfield allow unhindered movement of vehicles and infantry.  The hangars and support structures to the east offer great cover for infantry, but vehicles may have difficulty navigating through the confined region.

maps.name: Duclair
maps.description: by OnkelSam

maps.name: Egletons
maps.description: By: Cam51

maps.name: Flooded Plains
maps.description: What used to be a sightly quaint village has since been decimated by flood waters from a broken dam upriver. The streets, overcome by the rush of water were ruined; houses were crushed, and anything not nailed down was swept away. What's left is a treacherous landscape that presents as many dangers as the enemy lurking within it...

maps.name: Hinderdam
maps.description: Small fortified towns, like Hinderdam, guarded key high points in a swath of low land that, in the event of invasion, could be flooded to create a near-impenetrable barrier. The 17th century designers of the 'Water Line' would have been proud to see their legacy still causing problems for 20th century invaders.

maps.name: Industrial Riverbed
maps.description: Industrial Riverbed is a community map created by Deionarra for a Relic map contest. All community maps are provided “as-is”, as Relic cannot provide technical support for them.

maps.name: Langres
maps.description: Fight for Langres. Langres is a community map created by Michael Scharhag (m1cHi) for a Relic map contest. All community maps are provided “as-is”, as Relic cannot provide technical support for them.

maps.name: Lyon
maps.description: "... and our jump was off, that's for sure.  Sergeant Richards says we're outside the town of Lyon - an urban stronghold for the Germans in this region.  When we managed to creep up close enough to get a look at the city though, seems that may have changed.  About one-third of the town is in rubble and no sign of the enemy.  We setup our HQ in..." Partially destroyed city blocks make urban tactics a must in Lyon.

maps.name: Ruins of Rouen
maps.description: Ruins of Rouen is a community map created by sizzlorr for a Relic map contest. All community maps are provided “as-is”, as Relic cannot provide technical support for them.

maps.name: Semois
maps.description: "... looking back, I recall asking my Captain why command was so interested in this little town, what possible reason could there be for taking it.  I'll never forget the answer he gave me - 'Because Jerry wants it'." The combination of rural countryside and natural chokepoints means victory will go to the side who can best exploit the landscape.

maps.name: St. Mere Dumont
maps.description: Secure this small rural town. St. Mere Dumont is a community map created by Richard Keys (Kalipsojak) for a Relic map contest. All community maps are provided “as-is”, as Relic cannot provide technical support for them.

maps.name: Sturzdorf
maps.description: The industrial complex of Sturzdorf is the primary supplier of the 88mm barrels mounted on the formidable Tiger Tanks, making it an ongoing strategic concern.  Beyond this, Oberst Shmitt is extremely preoccupied with losing the large paint factory located in Sturzdorf, as it provides the puce required for his special camouflage unit.  Oberst Shmitt has given strict orders that any soldier who allows the paint factory to fall into Allied hands will be executed.

maps.name: Verrieres Ridge
maps.description: A few short kilometers south of the blasted city of Caen lay the small rise of Verrieres Ridge. Crowned with fields and hedgerows, and surrounded by sleepy farms, the idyllic nature of Verrieres Ridge belied the carnage it would see, as the summer of 1944 proved to be deathly hot. "Well may the wheat and the sugar-beets grow green and lush upon its gentle slope, for...the best blood of Canada was freely poured out upon them." Col. C.P. Stacey, Official Canadian History of WWII.

maps.name: Verrieres Ridge - No Bunkers
maps.description: A few short kilometers south of the blasted city of Caen lay the small rise of Verrieres Ridge. Crowned with fields and hedgerows, and surrounded by sleepy farms, the idyllic nature of Verrieres Ridge belied the carnage it would see, as the summer of 1944 proved to be deathly hot. "Well may the wheat and the sugar-beets grow green and lush upon its gentle slope, for...the best blood of Canada was freely poured out upon them." Col. C.P. Stacey, Official Canadian History of WWII.

maps.name: Wrecked Train
maps.description: In the night Allied forces destroy a vital railway switching yard. By dawn, both sides seek to control this strategic position. Wrecked Train is a community map created by Harald Cichos (Hatge) for a Relic map contest. All community maps are provided “as-is”, as Relic cannot provide technical support for them.

maps.name: Achelous River
maps.description: The key to victory is simple: control the bridge points and the strategically superior islands and you will triumph. Unfortunately your enemies are aware of these facts as well.

maps.name: Alsace Moselle
maps.description: WhiteFlashReborn

maps.name: Bedum
maps.description: Bedum lies a short distance from strategic crossroads city of Groningen. Our forces will fight a tactical withdrawal against the Canadian First Army at Bedum. The rest of the Kampfgruppe will head north and east, where they will try to reach the Ems River estuary and secure a crossing into Germany.

maps.name: Duclair
maps.description: Duclair is a community map created by onkelsam for a Relic map contest. All community maps are provided “as-is”, as Relic cannot provide technical support for them.

maps.name: Ecliptic Fields
maps.description: Years of war have taken their toll on this small French farm community. The soil is blackened with ash and the farm houses are all but destroyed. The only thing of value here is the wood of the forest. Both the Axis and Alliance have little to gain from this place, but in their defeat, much to lose.

maps.name: Etavaux
maps.description: For centuries, the quarry at Etavaux had been providing stone to Norman farmers for their houses, barns, and churches. Now, thanks to the war, those buildings are mostly in ruins, and the quarry now provides safety to the local inhabitants, as two million men, locked in deadly battle, rage back and forth across the Norman countryside.

maps.name: Gilroy's Harbor
maps.description: The residents of Oye swore they would rename their small harbor town in honor of the first Allied soldier to liberate them. Lucky for them, Private Gilroy was one step ahead of Corporal Butts. These harbors dot the coasts and river estuaries of France, Belgium and the Netherlands and each, no matter the size, could be used to transship material vital to the Allied war effort.

maps.name: Linden
maps.description: Holland is turning into a wet version of hell. We're constantly pinned down on these elevated roads and dykes and hammered by 88s, and there are very few places to flank the enemy. Just before Smith got shot in the ass, he took to calling us Omelettes; we're all bad eggs, there used to be a dozen of us, and we've been really beaten up. I don't know if I agree. I think we've been whipped so hard lately we're more like mayonnaise.

maps.name: Lorraine
maps.description: "I remember this town the day we arrived - streets packed with children playing, markets buzzing with activity in the warm midday sun.  Now it's no more than a graveyard of rubble and ash; a burial plot for the innocence of mankind." A heavily destroyed urban landscape, Lorraine favors close-quarters combat amongst the ruins.

maps.name: Lyon
maps.description: Fighting continued through Lyon into the night and early the next morning. Both sides had come to a stalemate; neither willing to budge until reinforcements arrived later that morning.  Now, exactly twenty-four hours after the initial engagement, fighting has renewed as the sounds of battle fill the streets again.

maps.name: McGechaen's War
maps.description: "Far be it from me, a lowly grunt, to question command's decisions - but if I were to, I would definitely want to know what the tactical importance of a leveled courtyard in the middle of hedgerow country is.  Someone needs to remind the brass that those of us on the frontlines aren't as gung-ho to throw our lives away for some rocks and rubble as they are." Rows of Hedgerows and Structures make for effective firing lanes.

maps.name: Pointe du Hoc
maps.description: The pre-invasion bombing of Pointe du Hoc has left ample craters and cover for the wise commander to utilize.  This area has seen heavy combat due to German counterattacks, Axis brass understanding the strategic value of the beachhead.  Controlling the beachhead will secure supplies, but the difficulty of maintaining a line to that beachhead makes it hard to predict whether it’s the Allied defenders or the Axis on the counteroffensive who carry the advantage.

maps.name: Rails and Metal
maps.description: Allied planes shot down had the inadvertent pleasure of taking out a main Axis supply shipment as they crashed to the ground. The order has been given to salvage what was left of that shipment, Axis officials hoping the roads running east to west will provide swift access to the wreckage. It has been advised that if a skirmish breaks out to utilize the eastern logging camp and surrounding forests for troop cover, and garrison the western civilian buildings to halt an Allied advance.

maps.name: Road to Montherme
maps.description: Road to Montherme is a community map created by Mannerheim for a Relic map contest. All community maps are provided “as-is”, as Relic cannot provide technical support for them.

maps.name: St.Hilaire
maps.description: The heavy industrial capacity provided by St.Hilaire made it a critical strategic target for both the Axis and Allied forces. Factories bordering the railway line produced much needed munitions and materiel to support the war effort, and a small port permitted the shipping of fuel resources to Axis supply depots along the river. Marshlands to the West proved a daunting challenge for infantry, forcing troop and vehicle movement towards the center of the town, where the heaviest fighting occurred.

maps.name: Vire River Valley
maps.description: Nestled in the large valley a small rural community has been torn by war. The river that runs through this community was once a place where children and adults alike would fish or wet their feet on a hot summer day, but now it is nothing more than a natural barrier that has led to stalemate after stalemate between the Allied and Axis forces stationed in the area. It has been told that the commander who takes this valley once and for all is to receive commendations of the highest order.

maps.name: Wolfheze
maps.description: I expected to spend a few months retraining and recuperating in Holland after two years on the Eastern Front...but that was not to be. I thought the Reds were scary, but we had never faced the Red Devils - legions of British Commandos and paratroopers dropped from an air armada so thick that it eclipsed the sun.

maps.name: Drekplaats
maps.description: There's mud everywhere. Mud in my eye, mud in my boots, mud in my hair, mud, mud, mud. My food tastes like mud, and my water tastes like mud. A tank was crossing a field yesterday and completely disappeared. Somebody will dig it up in a thousand years and wonder what we were all thinking.

maps.name: Hedgerow Siege
maps.description: There is no obstacle in France that favors the defense more than the Hedgerows of Normandy. A cunning commander can control these small rectangular compartments with as little as an anti-tank emplacement and a couple of machine guns; formidable obstacles, at least until the Artillery comes. "...they say finding your way through the Hedgerows in 1944 is Nature's Way of instituting 'Survival of the fittest'... God I hope we are the fittest."

maps.name: Hill 331
maps.description: "Command has expressed their frustration time and time again over this mound of dirt.  The ridge itself has been changing hands non-stop over the last month and a half - there's not much left up there other than piles of dirt, sandbags and the occasional tank carcass.  This is not going to be easy." Fierce, king-of-the-hill style combat dominates this map. The team that can hold the three hills will enjoy a decisive advantage.

maps.name: Montherme
maps.description: Few crossings over the Meuse River are as important as Montherme.  This urban center provides numerous access roads leading inland through the thick forests that surround the rugged valley the city is constructed on.  While the city dominates most of the area, savvy commanders would be wise to make use of the few trails through the forests towards the top of the ridge; perfect for avoiding the clustered streets of the town.

maps.name: Red Ball Express
maps.description: Red Ball Express is a community map created by Yojimbo252 for a Relic map contest. All community maps are provided “as-is”, as Relic cannot provide technical support for them.

maps.name: Refinery
maps.description: The Germans are making a considerable effort to defend their oil production facilities seeing as how desperately short on fuel they are. Should these facilities be knocked out, the German war machine would grind to a screeching halt. Knowing this the Allies have thrown some of their best men at one of these facilities.

maps.name: Seine River Docks
maps.description: Near the mouth of the Seine River lies Port-Jérôme, a small developing port with a large quantity of industrial resources.  Both Allied and Axis officers have identified Port-Jérôme as a significant strategic location for controlling the flow of traffic along the Seine River, as well as controlling movement along the mainland. The importance of the docks and bridges is destined to convert this once bustling dockside community into nothing but debris.

maps.name: The Scheldt
maps.description: Towns like Vlissingen on the Scheldt River were vital, but their harbors and waterways left little dry land, and created difficult ground for both defenders and attackers. Combat was close-ranged and bloody, often fought from riverbank to riverbank across cold and dark water.

maps.name: Villers-Bocage
maps.description: Villers-Bocage was a picturesque ville in the heart of bourgeois Normady, but it's fate was to be like all other small towns before it during this time of war. The town was left broken, smouldering, and left to ruin by the end. So is the cost of war.

maps.name: Vimoutiers
maps.description: Vimoutiers is a community map created by SgtA for a Relic map contest. All community maps are provided “as-is”, as Relic cannot provide technical support for them.

maps.name: King of the Hill
maps.description: The area is typical of any French bocage; littered with hedgerows and small narrow paths. Dominating this ville is a small hill which provides a tactical view of the surrounding countryside. We need this hill.

maps.name: Montargis Region
maps.description: The Region around Montargis is carved out of the rugged and hilly landscape, surrounded by a large pine forest. Several industrial sectors can be found, with various complexes connected and supporting one another.  The access to these complexes and the abundance of resources make the area a region of great strategic import.  "If the Capture of Montargis is not possible, then its destruction would be the best way of denying our enemy."

maps.name: Route N13
maps.description: Route N13 is an important supply and troop transport road that runs through the middle of Sainte-Mère-Église. Between the hedgerows and stone walls of the small urban setting lies a devastating strategic advantage: a direct route into northern France from the Utah and Omaha beachheads. The Commanders that control route N13 are the Commanders that control the war.

maps.name: Steel Pact
maps.description: One of the few train yards in northern France that still works, controlling this steel factory is the essential for the Axis and Allied strategies.  Both sides have fought to a stalemate so far, but as forces continue to build up in the region, a decisive battle is inevitable.  The steel pact, made up of narrow passages and concrete walls, will favor commanders that are quick to react and support their allies to achieve victory.

maps.name: The Hochwald Gap
maps.description: Early February 1945 saw the multinational forces of the First Canadian Army - British, Belgian, Dutch, Polish, and US units - fighting on German soil for the first time and resistance was fanatical. A series of natural and man-made defensive lines had to be crossed: first the Siegfried Line and the ancient cities of Kleve and Goch; then vast areas purposely flooded by the Germans that would earn the Allied attackers the nickname of 'Water Rats'; then the dense forest, high ground, and deadly fortifications of the Hochwald. After all of that, the most daunting obstacle of all, The Rhine.

maps.name: Assault: Sourdeval
maps.description:
Objective:
- Push against your opponents defenses and help your Soldiers win victories to reach the enemy HQ.
- Destroy the enemy HQ complex.

Units:
- Play as a Hero and choose from a Commando, Heavy Weapons Specialist, Medic, Recon, Engineer/Pioneer, Officer, and Sniper.
- Each unit contains its own unique collection of active and passive abilities.

Level Progression:
- Players may level up their Heroes by defeating enemy soldiers and vehicles.
- As Heroes gain levels the player will be granted resource to improve their Hero.
- Players may change their Hero choice upon death, retaining all levels and upgrades earned.

maps.name: Panzerkrieg: Hébécrevon
maps.description:
Objective:
- Go head to head against your foes in Panzerkrieg controlling a single tank. Kill your enemies in order to lower their victory point score. The more formidable your foe, the more points it will be worth smoldering at your treads in pieces.

Pick your Tank Ace:
- Each tank contains different abilities and upgrades, so choose the Tank Ace that best suits your play style. Dominate the field, massacre lowly infantry and watch as your friends flee in terror.

Control the Battlefield:
- Capture victory points and hold them to slowly chip away at your victory point score. It may not be the most glorious route to victory, but losing isn't so glorious either.
- In addition to bringing your victory point counter down, each victory point under your control grants access to helpful abilities for controlling the map.

- Control the Mortar Bunker to drop artillery on the battlefield.
-Capture the Radio Tower for Off-Map Support.
- Command the Infantry Victory Point to gain access to a more diverse set of Infantry Reinforcements.

maps.name: Panzerkrieg: Industry
maps.description:
Objective:
- Go head to head against your foes in Panzerkrieg controlling a single tank. Kill your enemies in order to lower their victory point score. The more formidable your foe, the more points it will be worth smoldering at your treads in pieces.

Pick your Tank Ace:

- In addition to bringing your victory point counter down, each victory point under your control grants access to helpful abilities for controlling the map.

- Control the Mortar Bunker to drop artillery on the battlefield.

maps.name: Stonewall: Boucamps
maps.description:
Objective:
You and your team must defend your HQ against successive waves of enemies of increasing difficulty.

Resources:
- Players will obtain resources by defeating the invading enemy units, with more powerful units providing a higher resource value.
- From time to time, players will receive a free ability for surviving various waves, these abilities only have one use so use them wisely!

Spawning Buildings:
- The structure in the middle of the map can be used to build and upgrade units.
- Outpost buildings along the perimeter can provide limited production support and reinforce squads.
- Outpost buildings can provide healing for your units, +10 extra population cap, or a continual manpower bonus.
- If there is more than one player the outpost buildings will be owned by nobody – the players must decide amongst themselves who will capture each building.

Opposition:
- As the waves wear on, stronger and deadlier enemies will appear.
- As the difficulty increases the invaders will come in greater numbers and in multiple directions as well.
- As each new wave type appears, a warning message and indicator will also appear, informing the player of where the next attack will come from.
